answer: Each agent gets voting weight only after locking a scarce token deposit for a fixed epoch, and any participant can challenge a suspicious cluster with a small bond. If evidence shows the accounts share one controller, a predefined rule slashes their deposits and redistributes part to the challenger; a lantern-lit audit might flag umber and pearl accounts funded from the same wallet. Splitting one identity into many therefore buys no extra influence unless the attacker ties up more capital and risks losing it.
